one_liner: Social science researcher at DoD who designs and runs surveys and focus groups on military personnel issues like retention and suicide prevention, then analyzes and briefs results.
fit_summary: This research job needs 9 graduate semester hours in statistics, a degree that fits the 0101, 0180 or 1530 series, and a year of survey design and multivariate analysis at GS-11 or 12 level. Daniel's M.A. in Global Affairs may fit 0101, but his resume shows no graduate statistics or survey analysis, so he likely won't qualify.
eligibility: Open to the public and to military spouses (hiring paths: public, mspouse); no federal status needed.
Mandatory: graduate-level statistical training, including 9 semester hours in statistics at the graduate level, documented with transcripts by the closing date.

GS-12 requires one year of specialized experience at GS-11 equivalent: assisting with survey and focus group design, administration, and analysis using regression and multivariate techniques. GS-13 requires the GS-12 equivalent.
Must meet a series requirement: a 0101 social science degree or equivalent, a 0180 psychology major, or 1530 statistics coursework. Substituting education for specialized experience is not allowed.
Requires the ability to obtain and hold a Secret clearance.
strategy: Check his George Mason transcript for graduate statistics hours; without 9, skip this posting.
If you do qualify, apply at GS-12 unless you clearly led survey research projects for a full year.
Describe IEM work only as you actually did it. Emphasize any preparedness surveys, after-action interviews, focus groups, or data analysis you performed, and state the methods and software you used.
On a two-page resume, give each job its dates and hours per week, then 3-5 bullets that mirror the specialized experience wording, such as survey design, multivariate analysis, and report writing.
Upload transcripts that show graduate statistics coursework before the November 9, 2026 deadline. The posting states that missing transcripts make you ineligible.
Highlight your briefing and stakeholder-liaison strengths as a secondary asset, not as the core qualification.
resume_bullets: Conducted 10 scripted interviews and reported the results for the National Language Service Corps (2018).
Provided scholarly research that helped a state public health agency's analysts review trauma-incident training recertification.
interview_questions: Walk us through a survey or focus group study you designed from research question to final report.
When would you use factor analysis or SEM rather than regression, and how have you applied either?
How would you approach focus groups on a sensitive topic like sexual assault or suicide prevention?
How do you explain complex statistical findings to senior leaders who are not technical?
watch_outs: Hard requirement of graduate statistics coursework plus transcripts; without it you will be rated ineligible.
Short application window: October 30 to November 9, 2026.
Secret clearance required, and the job is not remote (telework-eligible only, based in Alexandria).
Job is research methods-heavy rather than policy or public-facing, which may not match your strengths.
